title: Aeneid, Book 1
author: Publius Vergilius Maro (Virgil)
source_notes: Latin text: Mynors, Oxford Classical Text via Perseus. English: John Dryden 1697 via Perseus.
reading_notes: Book 1 of the Aeneid. 756 lines. Per-line latin with per-line gloss; John Dryden's prose translation provided as parallel panel for context.

lines.original: Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris
lines.english: I sing of arms and the man who first came from the shores of Troy
lines.gloss:
**Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris**

*arma* (n. acc. pl.) "arms, warfare"; *virum-que* (m. acc. sg.) "and the man" (acc. object of *cano*); *cano* (1st sg. pres. ind.) "I sing"; *Troiae* (f. gen. sg.) "of Troy"; *primus* (m. nom. sg.) "first"; *ab oris* (f. abl. pl.) "from the shores." The poet announces his dual theme—war and the hero who first came from Troy's coasts.

lines.original: Italiam, fato profugus, Laviniaque venit
lines.english: came to Italy, an exile by fate, and the Lavinian shores
lines.gloss:
**Italiam, fato profugus, Laviniaque venit**

*Italiam* (acc. sg., "Italy") – destination after *venit*; *fato* (abl. sg., "by fate") – ablative of cause; *profugus* (nom. sg. m., "exiled, fugitive") – predicative adjective describing the subject *qui*; *Laviniaque* (acc. pl. neut., "Lavinian [shores]") – *-que* coordinates with *litora* in the next line; *venit* (3rd sg. perf., "he came") – main verb. Aeneas, driven by destiny as an exile, reached Italy and the Lavinian coast.

lines.original: litora, multum ille et terris iactatus et alto
lines.english: shores, much tossed on lands and sea
lines.gloss:
**litora, multum ille et terris iactatus et alto**

*litora* (n. acc. pl., "shores"); *multum* (adv., "much, greatly"); *iactatus* (perf. pass. part., nom. sg. m., "having been tossed/driven"); *terris* (f. abl. pl., "on/by lands"); *alto* (n. abl. sg., "on/by the deep/sea"). The hero, much tossed both on lands and on the sea, reaches the shores of Italy, with *iactatus* governing the ablatives of place where.

lines.original: vi superum saevae memorem Iunonis ob iram;
lines.english: by the force of the gods above, on account of cruel Juno's unforgetting wrath
lines.gloss: **vi** (abl. sing. of *vis*) "by the force/violence"; **superum** (gen. pl. of *superi*) "of the gods above"; **saevae** (gen. sing. fem. of *saevus*) "of savage/cruel"; **memorem** (acc. sing. fem. of *memor*) "remembering/mindful"; **Iunonis** (gen. sing. of *Iuno*) "of Juno"; **iram** (acc. sing. of *ira*) "wrath/anger." The hero was tossed about by the violence of the gods above, on account of the wrath of savage Juno who remembered (her grievances).

lines.original: multa quoque et bello passus, dum conderet urbem,
lines.english: Having suffered much in war as well, until he could found the city
lines.gloss:
**multa** (acc. pl. neut., "many things") **quoque** ("also") **et** ("and") **bello** (abl. sg., "in/by war") **passus** (perf. part., "having suffered") **dum** ("while") **conderet** (imperf. subj., "he might found") **urbem** (acc. sg., "city").

Aeneas suffered many things also in war while he was founding his city. The subjunctive *conderet* with *dum* expresses contemporaneous action with the main verb *passus [est]*.

lines.original: inferretque deos Latio, genus unde Latinum,
lines.english: and bring his gods to Latium, whence came the Latin race,
lines.gloss:
**inferretque deos Latio, genus unde Latinum,**

*inferretque*: 3rd sg. impf. subj. act. of *inferre*, "and he might bring in/introduce"; *deos*: acc. pl. m., "the gods" (his household gods/Penates); *Latio*: dat. sg. of *Latium*, "into Latium"; *genus*: nom. sg. n., "the race/lineage"; *unde*: relative adv., "from which/whence"; *Latinum*: nom. sg. n. of *Latinus*, "Latin." Aeneas would bring his gods to Latium, from which the Latin race and Alban fathers would descend.

lines.original: Albanique patres, atque altae moenia Romae.
lines.english: and the Alban fathers and the walls of lofty Rome.
lines.gloss:
**Albanique patres, atque altae moenia Romae.**

*Albanique* (adj., nom. pl. masc., "Alban") modifies *patres* (noun, nom. pl., "fathers/senators"); *atque* (conj., "and") connects the two objects; *altae* (adj., gen. sg. fem., "lofty/high") modifies *Romae* (noun, gen. sg., "of Rome"); *moenia* (noun, nom./acc. pl. neut., "walls/fortifications"). This line completes the genealogical sequence from Troy to Rome, naming the Alban fathers (descendants of Aeneas through his son Ascanius who founded Alba Longa) and culminating in Rome's mighty walls as the destined outcome of Aeneas's journey.

lines.original: Musa, mihi causas memora, quo numine laeso,
lines.english: Muse, recall for me the causes, what divine will having been offended,
lines.gloss:
**Musa, mihi causas memora, quo numine laeso**

*Musa* (nom. sg., "Muse") is invoked in the imperative *memora* ("recall, recount"). *mihi* (dat. sg., "to me") indicates the indirect object. *causas* (acc. pl., "causes, reasons") is the direct object. *quo numine laeso* (abl. sg., "with what divinity offended/wounded") expresses attendant circumstances, with *laeso* as a perfect passive participle modifying *numine*.

lines.original: quidve dolens, regina deum tot volvere casus
lines.english: or what grief made the queen of the gods drive a man through so many misfortunes
lines.gloss:
**quidve dolens, regina deum tot volvere casus**

*quidve* (conjunction, "or what") connects alternative questions about divine motivation; *dolens* (present participle, nominative singular, "grieving") modifies *regina*; *regina deum* (nominative + genitive plural, "queen of the gods") refers to Juno; *volvere* (present active infinitive, "to roll/cause to revolve") governs *casus*; *tot casus* (accusative plural, "so many misfortunes") are the object of *volvere*. The line asks why Juno, grieving, compelled a pious hero to endure such repeated calamities.

lines.original: insignem pietate virum, tot adire labores
lines.english: compelled a man renowned for piety to undergo so many labors
lines.gloss:
**insignem pietate virum, tot adire labores**

*insignem* (acc. sg. m., adj. from *insignis*) = "distinguished, remarkable," modifying *virum*. *pietate* (abl. sg. f., noun from *pietas*) = "piety, devotion," ablative of respect. *virum* (acc. sg. m., noun from *vir*) = "man," object of *impulerit*. *tot* (indecl. adj.) = "so many," modifying *labores*. *adire* (pres. inf., verb from *adeo*) = "to undergo, approach," complementary infinitive with *impulerit*. *labores* (acc. pl. m., noun from *labor*) = "labors, hardships," object of *adire*. 

The line questions why Juno compelled a man distinguished for his piety to undergo so many

lines.original: impulerit. Tantaene animis caelestibus irae?
lines.english: Could such anger dwell in heavenly hearts?
lines.gloss: **impulerit** (perf. subj. act., 3rd sg. of *impello*) "drove" or "compelled"; **tantaene** (nom. pl. fem., interrogative adj. with enclitic *-ne*) "so great?"; **animis** (dat. pl. of *animus*) "in the minds/hearts"; **caelestibus** (dat. pl. of *caelestis*) "of the heavenly ones" or "celestial"; **irae** (nom. pl. of *ira*) "angers" or "wraths." The poet asks rhetorically what drove the goddess to inflict such suffering on pious Aeneas, questioning whether such great wraths exist in the hearts of the gods.

lines.original: Urbs antiqua fuit, Tyrii tenuere coloni,
lines.english: There was an ancient city, Tyrian colonists held it,
lines.gloss: **Urbs** (nom. sg. f.) "city"; **antiqua** (nom. sg. f. adj.) "ancient"; **fuit** (3rd sg. perf. act. ind. of *sum*) "was/there was"; **Tyrii** (nom. pl. m. adj.) "Tyrian"; **tenuere** (3rd pl. perf. act. ind. of *teneo*, syncopated form of *tenuerunt*) "held/occupied"; **coloni** (nom. pl. m.) "colonists/settlers." The line introduces Carthage as an ancient city held by Tyrian colonists, beginning Juno's backstory and her hostility toward the Trojans.

lines.original: Karthago, Italiam contra Tiberinaque longe
lines.english: Carthage, far opposite Italy and the Tiber's mouth
lines.gloss: **Karthago** (nom. sg., f.): Carthage, the ancient Phoenician city in North Africa. **Italiam** (acc. sg., f.): Italy, object of *contra*. **contra** (prep. + acc.): opposite to, facing. **Tiberina** (acc. pl., n.): Tiber-related things, here the mouths of the Tiber River. **longe** (adv.): far, at a distance. Carthage stood far opposite Italy and the Tiber's mouths.

lines.original: ostia, dives opum studiisque asperrima belli;
lines.english: rich in wealth and most fierce in the pursuits of war
lines.gloss: **ostia** (n. pl. acc.) "mouths" or "harbors" – the outlets of the Tiber river; **dives** (adj. nom. f. sg.) "rich"; **opum** (gen. pl. of *opes*) "in resources/wealth"; **studiis** (abl. pl.) "in pursuits/zeal"; **asperrima** (superl. adj. nom. f. sg.) "most fierce/savage"; **belli** (gen. sg.) "of war." Carthage stands geographically opposite Italy and the Tiber's mouths, rich in resources and supremely fierce in its warlike pursuits.

lines.original: quam Iuno fertur terris magis omnibus unam
lines.english: which Juno is said to have cherished above all other lands alone
lines.gloss: **quam** (relative pronoun, acc. sing. fem.) "which" refers to Carthage; **Iuno** (nom. sing.) "Juno"; **fertur** (3rd sing. pres. pass. indic. of *fero*) "is said/reported"; **magis** (adv.) "more"; **omnibus** (abl. pl. neut. with *terris*) "all." Juno is reported to have cherished this one city more than all other lands, with *posthabita...Samo* (abl. absolute) indicating "even Samos having been placed second."

lines.original: posthabita coluisse Samo; hic illius arma,
lines.english: having set aside Samos, she cherished this one; here were her arms,
lines.gloss:
**posthabita coluisse Samo; hic illius arma,**

*posthabita* (perfect passive participle, ablative singular feminine from *posthabeo*) "having been set aside/postponed," modifies *Samo*; *coluisse* (perfect active infinitive from *colo*) "to have cherished/cultivated," dependent on *fertur* from the previous line; *Samo* (ablative singular) "than Samos," ablative of comparison with *posthabita*; *arma* (nominative/accusative plural neuter) "arms/weapons." Juno cherished Carthage more than even Samos (her birthplace now set aside in favor); here were her arms/weapons.

lines.original: hic currus fuit; hoc regnum dea gentibus esse,
lines.english: Here was her chariot; here the goddess aimed that this should be a kingdom over nations.
lines.gloss:
**Target line: hic currus fuit; hoc regnum dea gentibus esse,**

*hic* (adverb) = here; *currus* (nom. sg. m.) = chariot; *fuit* (3rd sg. perf. act. indic. of *sum*) = was; *hoc* (acc. sg. n. demonstrative) = this; *regnum* (acc. sg. n.) = kingdom/dominion; *gentibus* (dat. pl. f.) = for the nations/peoples; *esse* (pres. act. infin. of *sum*) = to be. 

Juno's chariot was here (at Carthage); the goddess strives that this place be the ruling power over the nations, with *hoc regnum esse* as indirect statement dependent on *tendit* in the following line.

lines.original: si qua fata sinant, iam tum tenditque fovetque.
lines.english: if the fates would allow, even then she strove and cherished this aim.
lines.gloss:
**si qua fata sinant, iam tum tenditque fovetque.**

Key words: *si* (conj.) "if"; *fata* (n. nom./acc. pl., "fates") subject of *sinant*; *sinant* (pres. subj. 3rd pl. *sino*) "should allow/permit"; *tendit* (pres. indic. 3rd sg. *tendo*) "strives for, works toward"; *fovet* (pres. indic. 3rd sg. *foveo*) "cherishes, fosters." Juno already then (referring to Carthage's future supremacy) strives for and cherishes this destiny, if only the fates should permit it.

lines.original: Progeniem sed enim Troiano a sanguine duci
lines.english: But she had heard that a race was being drawn from Trojan blood
lines.gloss:
**Progeniem sed enim Troiano a sanguine duci**

*Progeniem* (acc. sing., "offspring/race") is the object of *audierat* (from the next line); *Troiano...a sanguine* (abl. of source with preposition, "from Trojan blood") indicates origin; *duci* (pres. pass. inf., "to be led/descended") completes the indirect statement. Juno had heard that a race descended from Trojan blood would one day overthrow the Tyrian citadels. *Sed enim* provides emphatic transition ("but indeed/for").

lines.original: audierat, Tyrias olim quae verteret arces;
lines.english: She had heard that a race sprung from Trojan blood would one day overthrow her Tyrian citadels.
lines.gloss:
**audierat, Tyrias olim quae verteret arces;**

*audierat* (pluperfect active indicative, 3rd sg. of *audio*) = "she had heard"; *Tyrias* (accusative plural feminine adjective modifying *arces*) = "Tyrian"; *olim* (adverb) = "one day, someday"; *quae* (nominative singular feminine relative pronoun, subject of *verteret*) = "which" (referring to *progeniem*); *verteret* (imperfect subjunctive, 3rd sg. of *verto*) = "would overthrow"; *arces* (accusative plural of *arx*) = "citadels, strongholds." Juno had heard that a Trojan-descended race would one day destroy the Tyrian citadels (i.e., Carthage in the Punic Wars).

lines.original: hinc populum late regem belloque superbum
lines.english: that from this would come a people ruling far and wide and proud in war
lines.gloss:
**hinc** (adv., "from this source/hence") **populum** (acc. sing. m., "a people/nation") **late** (adv., "widely") **regem** (acc. sing. m., "ruling") **belloque** (abl. sing. n., "and in war") **superbum** (acc. sing. m., "proud/mighty"). 

Juno had heard that a people ruling widely and proud in war would come from this Trojan source to destroy her beloved Carthage; *populum* is the object of *venturum* (in the next line), with *regem* and *superbum* as predicative adjectives describing Rome's future dominance.

lines.original: venturum excidio Libyae: sic volvere Parcas.
lines.english: that would come for the destruction of Libya: thus the Fates were spinning.
lines.gloss: **venturum** (acc. sg. m. fut. act. participle of *venio*) "about to come"; **excidio** (dat. sg. of *excidium*) "for/to the destruction"; **Libyae** (gen. or dat. sg. of *Libya*) "of/to Libya"; **volvere** (pres. act. inf. of *volvo*) "to roll, unroll, ordain"; **Parcas** (acc. pl. of *Parca*) "the Fates." Juno fears that this people (the Romans) will come for the destruction of Libya (Carthage), as the Fates were spinning/decreeing it.

lines.original: Id metuens, veterisque memor Saturnia belli,
lines.english: Fearing this, and remembering the old war, the daughter of Saturn
lines.gloss:
**Id metuens, veterisque memor Saturnia belli,**

*Id* (demonstrative pronoun, neuter accusative singular) = "that," object of *metuens*; *metuens* (present participle of *metuo*, nominative singular) = "fearing"; *veteris* (adjective, genitive singular) = "old, former," modifying *belli*; *memor* (adjective + genitive) = "mindful of, remembering"; *Saturnia* (adjective/epithet, nominative singular) = "daughter of Saturn," i.e., Juno; *belli* (noun, genitive singular) = "of the war," referring to the Trojan War. Juno, fearing this prophesied destruction of Carthage and remembering her old warfare at Troy, prepares her opposition to the Trojans.

lines.original: prima quod ad Troiam pro caris gesserat Argis—
lines.english: which she had first waged at Troy for her beloved Argos
lines.gloss:
**prima quod ad Troiam pro caris gesserat Argis—**

*prima* (nom. sg. fem., "first" or "foremost," modifying Saturnia): Juno as the principal actor. *quod* (conjunction, "because"): introduces a causal clause explaining her hostility. *gesserat* (pluperfect active, 3rd sg., from *gero*, "to wage/conduct"): she had waged. *pro caris...Argis* (preposition + abl., "on behalf of dear/beloved Argos"): for Greece in the Trojan War. The line recalls Juno's partisan role supporting the Greeks against Troy.

lines.original: necdum etiam causae irarum saevique dolores
lines.english: nor yet had the causes of her wrath and bitter resentments fallen from her mind
lines.gloss:
**necdum etiam causae irarum saevique dolores**

*necdum* (adv.) = "not yet"; *causae* (nom. pl., f.) = "causes"; *irarum* (gen. pl., f.) = "of her anger/wrath"; *saevi* (gen. sg., m./n. or nom. pl., m.) = "of cruel/savage" (modifying *dolores*); *dolores* (nom. pl., m.) = "griefs, resentments." The line continues the explanation of Juno's hostility: not yet had the causes of her anger and cruel grievances departed from her mind.

lines.original: exciderant animo: manet alta mente repostum
lines.english: had fallen from her mind: there remained stored deep in her heart
lines.gloss: **exciderant** (pluperfect active indicative, 3rd pl. of *excido*) "had fallen out/away," **animo** (ablative of separation) "from [her] mind," **manet** (present active indicative, 3rd sg. of *maneo*) "remains," **alta mente repostum** (ablative of place where + neuter nominative/accusative sg. perfect passive participle of *repono*) "stored deep in [her] mind." The causes of Juno's anger had not yet fallen from her mind; the judgment remains deeply stored within her.

lines.original: iudicium Paridis spretaeque iniuria formae,
lines.english: The judgment of Paris and the injury of her scorned beauty
lines.gloss:
**iudicium Paridis spretaeque iniuria formae**

*iudicium* (nom. n. sg., "judgment") refers to Paris's award of the golden apple; *Paridis* (gen. m. sg., "of Paris") possessive genitive; *spretae* (gen. f. sg., perf. pass. partic. of *sperno*, "scorned/rejected") modifies *formae*; *iniuria* (nom. f. sg., "insult/injury"); *formae* (gen. f. sg., "of beauty") objective genitive. Juno recalls Paris's judgment that spurned her beauty in favor of Venus, a lasting source of divine wrath.

lines.original: et genus invisum, et rapti Ganymedis honores.
lines.english: and the hated race, and the honors of ravished Ganymede.
lines.gloss:
**et genus invisum, et rapti Ganymedis honores.**

*genus* (n. nom./acc. sg.): "race, offspring" (referring to the Trojan people); *invisum* (adj. nom./acc. sg. n.): "hated"; *rapti* (perf. pass. part. gen. sg. m.): "seized, abducted"; *Ganymedis* (m. gen. sg.): "of Ganymede" (Trojan youth abducted by Jupiter to be cupbearer); *honores* (m. nom./acc. pl.): "honors, privileges." Juno's rage is further inflamed by her hatred of the Trojan race and her resentment over the honors given to the abducted Ganymede, who supplanted Juno's daughter Hebe as cupbearer to the gods.

lines.original: His accensa super, iactatos aequore toto
lines.english: Inflamed by these things moreover, she kept tossing over the whole sea the Trojans.
lines.gloss:
**His accensa super, iactatos aequore toto**

*His* (ablative plural, demonstrative pronoun) "by these things"; *accensa* (nominative feminine singular, perfect passive participle of *accendo*) "inflamed, enraged"; *super* (adverb) "in addition, moreover"; *iactatos* (accusative masculine plural, perfect passive participle of *iacto*) "storm-tossed, harried"; *aequore* (ablative singular of *aequor*) "over/on the sea"; *toto* (ablative singular of *totus*) "all, whole." Juno, inflamed moreover by these grievances, drove the Trojans who had been tossed over the entire sea.

lines.original: Troas, reliquias Danaum atque immitis Achilli,
lines.english: The Trojans, remnants left by the Greeks and pitiless Achilles
lines.gloss:
**Troas, reliquias Danaum atque immitis Achilli,**

*Troas* (acc. pl. m., "Trojans") is the direct object continued from the previous line's *arcebat*. *reliquias* (acc. pl. f., "remnants, survivors") stands in apposition to *Troas*. *Danaum* (gen. pl. m., "of the Greeks") is an objective genitive with *reliquias*. *immitis* (gen. sg. m./f., "pitiless, cruel") modifies *Achilli* (gen. sg. m., "of Achilles"), both dependent on *reliquias*—the Trojans are survivors of both the Greeks generally and savage Achilles specifically.

lines.original: arcebat longe Latio, multosque per annos
lines.english: She kept them far from Latium, and for many years
lines.gloss:
**arcebat longe Latio, multosque per annos**

*arcebat* (imperfect active, 3rd sg. of *arceo*) "was keeping away"; *longe* (adverb) "far"; *Latio* (ablative of separation with *Latium*) "from Latium"; *multosque* (accusative plural masculine of *multus*) "and for many"; *annos* (accusative plural of *annus*) "years." Juno was keeping the Trojans far from Latium for many years as they wandered the seas driven by fate.

lines.original: errabant, acti fatis, maria omnia circum.
lines.english: They wandered, driven by fate, around all the seas for many years.
lines.gloss:
**errabant, acti fatis, maria omnia circum.**

*errabant* (3rd pl. imperf. act. indic. of *erro*, "they were wandering"); *acti* (perf. pass. part. nom. pl. m. of *ago*, "driven"); *fatis* (abl. pl. of *fatum*, "by the fates"); *maria omnia* (acc. pl. neut., "all the seas"); *circum* (adv./prep., "around"). The Trojans wandered all the seas around, driven by the fates—emphasizing their prolonged suffering and divine compulsion before founding Rome.

lines.original: Tantae molis erat Romanam condere gentem!
lines.english: So great a task it was to found the Roman race!
lines.gloss: **Tantae** (gen. sg. f. adj., modifying *molis*) "of such great"; **molis** (gen. sg. f. noun, predicate genitive) "effort, toil, massive undertaking"; **erat** (3rd sg. imperf. act. ind., *sum*) "it was"; **Romanam** (acc. sg. f. adj., modifying *gentem*) "Roman"; **condere** (pres. act. inf., *condo*) "to found, establish"; **gentem** (acc. sg. f. noun) "race, nation." This famous editorial intrusion declares the immense difficulty required to found the Roman people, employing a genitive of quality construction with the impersonal verb.

lines.original: Vix e conspectu Siculae telluris in altum
lines.english: Scarcely out of sight of the Sicilian land into the deep
lines.gloss: **Vix** (adverb): "scarcely," "barely." **conspectu** (masculine noun, ablative singular of *conspectus*): "sight," "view." **Siculae** (adjective, genitive singular feminine, modifying *telluris*): "Sicilian." **telluris** (feminine noun, genitive singular of *tellus*): "land," "earth." **altum** (neuter noun, accusative singular of *altum*): "the deep (sea)," "the open waters." The Trojans had barely sailed out of sight of Sicilian land into the deep sea when Juno's intervention begins.

lines.original: vela dabant laeti, et spumas salis aere ruebant,
lines.english: They joyfully set sail and plowed through the salt spray with bronze.
lines.gloss:
**vela dabant laeti, et spumas salis aere ruebant,**

*vela* (n. acc. pl., "sails") *dabant* (imperf. act. ind., "were setting/giving") *laeti* (adj. nom. pl. m., "joyful") *spumas* (n. acc. pl., "foam") *salis* (n. gen. sg., "of salt/sea") *aere* (n. abl. sg., "with bronze," i.e., bronze-fitted prows) *ruebant* (imperf. act. ind., "were plowing/churning"). The Trojans joyfully set sail from Sicily, their bronze-beaked ships churning the sea's foam, just before Juno's intervention.

lines.original: cum Iuno, aeternum servans sub pectore volnus,
lines.english: when Juno, nursing an eternal wound deep in her heart,
lines.gloss:
**cum Iuno, aeternum servans sub pectore volnus,**

*cum* (conjunction) "when"; *Iuno* (nom. sg.) "Juno" (subject); *aeternum* (acc. sg. neut. adj.) "eternal," modifying *volnus*; *servans* (pres. part. nom. sg.) "keeping, preserving"; *sub pectore* (abl. of place) "beneath her breast, in her heart"; *volnus* (acc. sg. neut.) "wound." The goddess nurses an undying grievance as she observes the Trojans' progress.

lines.original: Mene incepto desistere victam, haec secum:
lines.english: Shall I desist defeated from my undertaking, she said to herself:
lines.gloss: **Mene** (acc. pronoun, "me") **incepto** (abl. neut. sing., "from my undertaking/purpose") **desistere** (pres. inf., "to cease/desist") **victam** (acc. fem. sing. perf. pass. part., "conquered/defeated") **haec secum** (acc. neut. pl. pron. + reflex. abl., "these things with herself"). Juno deliberates indignantly whether she, defeated, should abandon her enterprise; *haec secum* introduces her internal monologue, and the -ne enclitic marks the rhetorical question.

lines.original: nec posse Italia Teucrorum avertere regem?
lines.english: and not be able to turn away the Trojan king from Italy?
lines.gloss:
**Target line:** *nec posse Italia Teucrorum avertere regem?*

**Key words:** *nec* (negative conjunction, "nor/and not"); *posse* (present infinitive of possum, "to be able"); *Italia* (ablative of separation, "from Italy"); *Teucrorum* (genitive plural, "of the Trojans"); *avertere* (present infinitive, "to turn away/repel"); *regem* (accusative singular, "the king").

Juno protests that she cannot prevent the Trojan king from reaching Italy, questioning why Pallas could destroy the Greek fleet but she is forbidden by the fates to act similarly.

lines.original: Quippe vetor fatis. Pallasne exurere classem
lines.english: Of course I am forbidden by the fates. Yet could Pallas burn the fleet of the Argives
lines.gloss:
**Quippe vetor fatis. Pallasne exurere classem**

*quippe* (adv.) = "indeed, forsooth" (ironic); *vetor* (1st sg. pres. pass. indic., *veto*) = "I am forbidden"; *fatis* (abl. pl., *fatum*) = "by the fates"; *Pallas* (nom. sg.) = "Pallas (Athena)"; *exurere* (pres. act. inf., *exuro*) = "to burn up"; *classem* (acc. sg., *classis*) = "fleet." Juno protests bitterly that she is constrained by fate, while Pallas was permitted to incinerate the Greek fleet (for Ajax's sacrilege).

lines.original: Argivum atque ipsos potuit submergere ponto,
lines.english: Pallas was able to burn the Argive fleet and sink the men themselves in the sea.
lines.gloss: **Argivum** (adj. acc. masc. sing.) "Greek/Argive," modifying *classem* from the previous line; **ipsos** (intensive pron. acc. masc. plur.) "themselves," referring to the Greek warriors; **potuit** (perf. 3rd sing. of *possum*) "was able"; **submergere** (pres. act. inf. of *submergo*) "to sink, submerge"; **ponto** (abl. masc. sing. of *pontus*) "in/by the sea." Juno indignantly recalls that Pallas Athena could both burn the Greek fleet and drown the warriors themselves in the sea for the crime of one man, Ajax Oileus.

lines.original: unius ob noxam et furias Aiacis Oilei?
lines.english: for the crime and frenzy of Ajax son of Oileus alone?
lines.gloss: **unius** (adj., gen. sg., "of one") **ob** (prep. + acc., "on account of") **noxam** (noun, acc. sg., "crime, offense") **furias** (noun, acc. pl., "mad rage, frenzy") **Aiacis Oilei** (proper nouns, gen. sg., "of Ajax, son of Oileus"). Juno protests that she could destroy the entire Greek fleet on account of one man's crime and the mad violence of Ajax the Lesser (who raped Cassandra at Athena's altar).

lines.original: Ipsa, Iovis rapidum iaculata e nubibus ignem,
lines.english: She herself hurled swift fire of Jove from the clouds
lines.gloss:
**Ipsa, Iovis rapidum iaculata e nubibus ignem,**

*Ipsa* (intensive pronoun, nom. sing. fem.): "she herself" (Juno, emphatic subject). *Iovis* (noun, gen. sing.): "of Jove/Jupiter" (possessive, modifying *ignem*). *rapidum* (adj., acc. sing. masc.): "swift, snatching" (modifying *ignem*). *iaculata* (perfect participle, nom. sing. fem.): "having hurled" (from *iaculor*, describing Juno's action). *nubibus* (noun, abl. plur.): "from the clouds" (ablative of separation with *e*). *ignem* (noun, acc. sing. masc.): "thunderbolt, fire" (direct object of *iaculata*). 

Juno herself

lines.original: disiecitque rates evertitque aequora ventis,
lines.english: She scattered the ships and overturned the seas with winds.
lines.gloss:
**disiecitque rates evertitque aequora ventis**

*disiecit* (perf. ind. act. 3rd sg. of *disicio*) "scattered"; *rates* (acc. pl. f.) "ships, rafts"; *evertit* (perf. ind. act. 3rd sg. of *everto*) "overturned, upheaved"; *aequora* (acc. pl. n.) "seas, waters"; *ventis* (abl. pl. m.) "with/by winds." Juno (continuing from *ipsa*) both scattered the ships and churned up the seas with storm winds, intensifying the destruction wrought by her thunderbolt.

lines.original: illum expirantem transfixo pectore flammas
lines.english: Him breathing flames from his pierced breast she seized in a whirlwind and impaled on a jagged rock.
lines.gloss:
**illum** (acc. sg. m. of *ille*) "that one" / "him" – direct object of *corripuit* (from the next line), referring to a specific Greek warrior. **expirantem** (pres. part. acc. sg. m. of *exspiro*) "breathing out" – modifying *illum*. **transfixo pectore** (abl. sg. n. of *transfigo* + *pectus*) "with pierced chest" – ablative absolute. **flammas** (acc. pl. f. of *flamma*) "flames" – direct object of *expirantem*. 

The line depicts a warrior breathing out flames from his pierced chest, creating a vivid image of destruction during the storm or battle scene.

lines.original: turbine corripuit scopuloque infixit acuto.
lines.english: She seized him in a whirlwind and impaled him on a jagged rock.
lines.gloss: **turbine** (abl. sing., m., "whirlwind, storm") **corripuit** (3rd sing. perf. act., "seized, snatched up") **scopuloque** (abl. sing., m., "cliff, rock") **infixit** (3rd sing. perf. act., "fastened, impaled") **acuto** (abl. sing., m., "sharp, pointed"). Juno recounts how she seized Aeneas's ship in a whirlwind and dashed it upon a sharp crag, expressing her vengeful power against the Trojans.

lines.original: Ast ego, quae divom incedo regina, Iovisque
lines.english: But I, who walk as queen of the gods and Jove's both sister and wife
lines.gloss:
**Ast ego, quae divom incedo regina, Iovisque**

*Ast* (conjunction, "but"); *ego* (nominative pronoun, "I"); *quae* (nominative relative pronoun, "who"); *divom* (archaic genitive plural of *dī*, "of the gods"); *incedo* (1st sg. present indicative, "I walk/proceed"); *regina* (nominative, "queen"); *Iovisque* (*Iovis* genitive + *-que*, "and of Jupiter"). Juno bitterly contrasts her divine status as queen of the gods and Jupiter's consort with her inability to prevent Aeneas's success.

lines.original: et soror et coniunx, una cum gente tot annos
lines.english: both sister and wife, wage war with a single nation for so many years!
lines.gloss:
**et soror et coniunx, una cum gente tot annos**

Key words: *soror* (nom. sg. f., "sister"), *coniunx* (nom. sg. f., "wife/spouse"), *una* (adv., "together"), *gente* (abl. sg. f., "race/people"), *annos* (acc. pl. m., "years"). Juno identifies herself emphatically as both sister and wife of Jupiter, expressing her prolonged struggle against a single people (the Trojans) for so many years.

lines.original: bella gero! Et quisquam numen Iunonis adoret
lines.english: I wage wars! And will anyone worship Juno's divinity hereafter, or as a suppliant place offerings on her altars?
lines.gloss:
**bella gero! Et quisquam numen Iunonis adoret**

*bella* (n. acc. pl. of *bellum*) "wars"; *gero* (1st sg. pres. indic. of *gerere*) "I wage"; *quisquam* (nom. sg. indef. pron.) "anyone"; *numen* (n. acc. sg. of *numen*) "divinity, divine power"; *Iunonis* (gen. sg. of *Iuno*) "of Juno"; *adoret* (3rd sg. pres. subj. of *adorare*) "worship, adore." Juno bitterly asks whether anyone will still worship her divine power after she wages wars (yet fails to prevent Trojan success).

lines.original: praeterea, aut supplex aris imponet honorem?
lines.english: Or thereafter as a suppliant place offerings of honor upon her altars?
lines.gloss: **praeterea** (adv.) "hereafter, in the future"; **supplex** (adj., nom. sg.) "suppliant, as a suppliant"; **aris** (n., dat./abl. pl. of *ara*) "on/to the altars"; **imponet** (v., fut. 3rd sg. of *imponere*) "will place"; **honorem** (n., acc. sg. of *honor*) "honor, offering." Juno asks rhetorically whether any mortal will still worship her by placing votive offerings on her altars as a suppliant, given her apparent impotence to prevent the Trojans' success.

lines.original: Talia flammato secum dea corde volutans
lines.english: Revolving such thoughts in her heart aflame, the goddess
lines.gloss:
**Talia flammato secum dea corde volutans**

*Talia* (neut. pl. acc., "such things") is the object of *volutans* (pres. part. nom. sg. fem., "turning over, pondering"), describing *dea* (nom. sg. fem., "goddess," i.e., Juno). *Flammato...corde* (abl. sg. neut., "with inflamed heart") is an ablative of means/manner, depicting her emotional state. *Secum* ("with herself, within herself") emphasizes her internal deliberation. Juno broods over these grievances with burning rage before journeying to Aeolus's storm-realm.

lines.original: nimborum in patriam, loca feta furentibus austris,
lines.english: to the homeland of storm-clouds, a place teeming with raging south winds
lines.gloss: **nimborum** (gen. pl., "of storm-clouds") **in patriam** (acc. sg., "into the fatherland/homeland") **loca** (acc. pl., "places") **feta** (acc. pl. neuter, perf. part. of *feto*, "teeming/pregnant with") **furentibus austris** (abl. pl., "with raging south winds"). Juno arrives at Aeolia, the homeland of storm-clouds, a region teeming with wild southern gales under Aeolus' control.

lines.original: Aeoliam venit. Hic vasto rex Aeolus antro
lines.english: She came to Aeolia. Here in a vast cavern king Aeolus
lines.gloss: **Aeoliam** (adj. acc. sg. f., "Aeolian") modifies an understood *terram*; **venit** (3rd sg. pres./perf. indic., "comes/came"); **Hic** (adv., "here"); **vasto** (adj. abl. sg. n., "vast") modifies **antro** (abl. sg., "in a cave"); **rex** (nom. sg., "king") **Aeolus** (nom. sg., proper name). Aeneas arrives at Aeolia, where King Aeolus rules from his enormous cavern.

lines.original: luctantes ventos tempestatesque sonoras
lines.english: rules over the struggling winds and roaring storms with his command
lines.gloss:
**luctantes ventos tempestatesque sonoras**

*luctantes* (pres. act. participle, acc. masc. pl. from *luctor*) "struggling"; *ventos* (acc. masc. pl. of *ventus*) "winds"; *tempestatesque* (*-que* enclitic "and" + acc. fem. pl. of *tempestas*) "storms"; *sonoras* (acc. fem. pl. of *sonorus, -a, -um*) "roaring, thunderous." Aeolus controls the struggling winds and roaring storms within his vast cave through his power and restraints.

lines.original: imperio premit ac vinclis et carcere frenat.
lines.english: He subdues them with his command and restrains them with chains and prison.
lines.gloss: **imperio** (n., abl. sing.) "by command/authority"; **premit** (3rd sing. pres. act. indic. of *premo*) "presses down, restrains"; **vinclis** (n., abl. pl.) "with chains/bonds"; **carcere** (n., abl. sing.) "with prison/confinement"; **frenat** (3rd sing. pres. act. indic. of *freno*) "bridles, curbs." Aeolus restrains the struggling winds by his sovereign command, binding them with chains and confining them in their prison-cave.

lines.original: Illi indignantes magno cum murmure montis
lines.english: They, indignant, roar around the barriers with a great rumbling of the mountain.
lines.gloss:
**Illi indignantes magno cum murmure montis**

*Illi* (nom. pl. masc., "those [winds]"), *indignantes* (pres. part. nom. pl., "raging/chafing indignantly"), *magno* (abl. sg. neut., "with great"), *murmure* (abl. sg., "roar/rumbling"), *montis* (gen. sg., "of the mountain"). The imprisoned winds rage indignantly with a great roar within the mountain, their fury contained by Aeolus's barriers.

lines.original: circum claustra fremunt; celsa sedet Aeolus arce
lines.english: They roar around their barriers; Aeolus sits on his lofty citadel.
lines.gloss:
**circum claustra fremunt; celsa sedet Aeolus arce**

*circum* (prep. + acc.): around; *claustra* (n. acc. pl.): barriers, enclosures; *fremunt* (3rd pl. pres. indic.): they roar, rage; *celsa* (abl. fem. sg.): on/in the lofty; *arce* (abl. fem. sg.): citadel, height. The winds roar around their prison while Aeolus sits enthroned on his high citadel, controlling them before he soothes their fury.

lines.original: sceptra tenens, mollitque animos et temperat iras.
lines.english: holding his scepter, and he soothes their spirits and tempers their rage.
lines.gloss: **sceptra** (n. acc. pl., "scepter") **tenens** (pres. part. nom. sg., "holding"), **mollitque** (verb 3rd sg. pres., "and softens"), **animos** (m. acc. pl., "spirits/tempers"), **temperat** (verb 3rd sg. pres., "restrains/moderates"), **iras** (f. acc. pl., "angers/rages"). Aeolus sits in his lofty citadel holding his scepter of authority, soothing the spirits of the winds and controlling their violent rages.

lines.original: Ni faciat, maria ac terras caelumque profundum
lines.english: Were he not to do so, the seas and lands and deep heaven would be swept away.
lines.gloss:
**Ni faciat, maria ac terras caelumque profundum**

*Ni* (conjunction, "if not, unless") introduces a contrary-to-fact condition; *faciat* (3rd sg. pres. subj. of *facio*, "he does/makes") continues the subjunctive construction; *maria* (nom./acc. pl. neut. of *mare*, "seas"), *terras* (acc. pl. fem. of *terra*, "lands"), and *caelum* (acc. sg. neut. of *caelum*, "sky/heaven") with *profundum* (acc. sg. neut. adj., "deep, profound") form a cosmic triad of objects.

lines.original: quippe ferant rapidi secum verrantque per auras.
lines.english: The swift winds would indeed carry them off and sweep them through the air.
lines.gloss:
**quippe** (adverb): "indeed," "for certainly" – causal/explanatory particle justifying the preceding statement.

**ferant** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. subj., *fero*): "they would carry" – potential subjunctive expressing what the winds would do.

**rapidi** (adj., nom. pl. masc., *rapidus*): "rushing," "violent" – modifies the implied subject (winds).

**secum** (prep. + pron.): "with themselves" – *se* + *cum*, indicating what they sweep along together.

**verrant** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. subj., *verro*): "sweep away," "brush along" – paired with *ferant* to describe the destructive force of the unleashed winds through the air (*per auras*).

lines.original: Sed pater omnipotens speluncis abdidit atris,
lines.english: But the almighty Father hid them away in dark caverns,
lines.gloss:
**Sed pater omnipotens speluncis abdidit atris**

*pater* (nom. sg. m.): "father" (i.e., Jupiter); *omnipotens* (nom. sg. m.): "all-powerful," "almighty"; *speluncis* (abl. pl. f.): "in caves"; *abdidit* (perf. 3rd sg.): "hid," "concealed" (from *abdo*); *atris* (abl. pl. f.): "dark," "black." Jupiter, fearing the destructive power of the winds, concealed them in dark caverns.

lines.original: hoc metuens, molemque et montis insuper altos
lines.english: fearing this, and heaped a mass and lofty mountains above them
lines.gloss:
**hoc metuens, molemque et montis insuper altos**

*hoc* (neuter accusative singular, demonstrative pronoun): "this," object of *metuens*. *metuens* (present active participle, nominative singular from *metuo*): "fearing." *molemque* (feminine accusative singular noun with enclitic *-que*): "mass" or "massive structure," coordinated object. *montis* (masculine accusative plural noun): "mountains." *insuper* (adverb): "on top," "above." *altos* (masculine accusative plural adjective): "high," modifying *montis*. Jupiter, fearing this threat, imprisoned the winds beneath a massive barrier and high mountains piled on top.

lines.original: imposuit, regemque dedit, qui foedere certo
lines.english: He placed them over and gave them a king who under fixed compact would know to restrain or loosen the reins as commanded.
lines.gloss:
**imposuit**: perfect active indicative, 3rd singular of *impono*, "he placed (upon)" or "imposed."
**regemque**: accusative singular of *rex*, coordinated with *molem*, "and a king."
**dedit**: perfect active indicative, 3rd singular of *do*, "he gave."
**foedere certo**: ablative of means, *foedus* with *certus*, "by/under a fixed compact" or "by a sure covenant."

Jupiter imposed (the mass and mountains) and gave a king who would know, under fixed terms, to restrain and to slacken the reins.

lines.original: et premere et laxas sciret dare iussus habenas.
lines.english: who would know to tighten or to slacken the reins at command.
lines.gloss: **premere** (infinitive, "to restrain/press"), **laxas** (acc. pl. fem. adj., "loose/slack"), **sciret** (impf. subj., "would know how"), **habenas** (acc. pl. fem., "reins"). Jupiter appointed a king who would know how to tighten control and slacken the reins as commanded, governing under fixed treaty terms.

lines.original: Ad quem tum Iuno supplex his vocibus usa est:
lines.english: To him then Juno in supplication spoke with these words:
lines.gloss:
**Ad quem tum Iuno supplex his vocibus usa est:**

*Ad quem* (preposition + accusative relative pronoun) "to whom"; *Iuno* (nominative singular) "Juno," subject; *supplex* (nominative singular adjective) "suppliant, as a suppliant"; *vocibus* (ablative plural, *vox*) "with words/speech"; *usa est* (perfect deponent, *utor* + ablative) "used, employed." Juno approaches Aeolus in the posture of a supplicant, employing carefully chosen words to secure his aid.

lines.original: Aeole, namque tibi divom pater atque hominum rex
lines.english: Aeolus, for to you the father of the gods and king of men has given
lines.gloss: **Aeole**: vocative singular, addressing Aeolus, god of the winds. **tibi**: dative singular of *tu*, "to you." **divom**: archaic genitive plural of *deus* (= *deorum*), "of the gods." **pater**: nominative singular, "father," in apposition to *rex*. **rex**: nominative singular, "king," subject of an implied verb; together with *pater*, this phrase refers to Jupiter, who grants authority to Aeolus.

lines.original: et mulcere dedit fluctus et tollere vento ,
lines.english: and gave the power to calm the waves and raise them with the wind
lines.gloss:
**Target line:** *et mulcere dedit fluctus et tollere vento*

**Gloss:** *mulcere* (pres. act. inf., "to calm/soothe") and *tollere* (pres. act. inf., "to raise/lift") are complementary infinitives dependent on *dedit* (perf. act. ind. 3rd sg. of *do*, "he gave/granted"). *fluctus* (acc. pl. m., "waves") is the object of both infinitives, while *vento* (abl. sg. m., "by/with wind") is ablative of means. Jupiter has granted Aeolus the power both to calm the waves and to raise them by means of wind.

lines.original: gens inimica mihi Tyrrhenum navigat aequor,
lines.english: A race hostile to me sails the Tyrrhenian sea.
lines.gloss:
**gens inimica mihi Tyrrhenum navigat aequor**

*gens* (nom. sg. f.) "race, people"; *inimica* (nom. sg. f. adj.) "hostile" (with dat. *mihi* "to me"); *Tyrrhenum* (acc. sg. n. adj.) "Tyrrhenian, Etruscan"; *navigat* (3rd sg. pres. act. ind.) "sails across"; *aequor* (acc. sg. n.) "sea, plain of water." 

Juno complains that a race hostile to her is sailing the Tyrrhenian Sea (between Italy and Sicily), carrying Troy's conquered gods to Italy.

lines.original: Ilium in Italiam portans victosque Penates:
lines.english: carrying Troy to Italy and their conquered household gods
lines.gloss:
**Ilium** (acc. sg., neut.) "Troy" – **in** + **Italiam** (acc. sg., fem.) "into Italy" – **portans** (pres. part., nom. sg.) "carrying" – **victos** (perf. pass. part., acc. pl., masc.) "conquered" – **Penates** (acc. pl., masc.) "household gods."

Juno describes Aeneas bearing Troy and its defeated Penates toward Italy, emphasizing the persistence of the conquered Trojan legacy that she seeks to destroy.

lines.original: incute vim ventis submersasque obrue puppes,
lines.english: Hurl force into the winds and overwhelm their submerged ships.
lines.gloss:
**incute vim ventis submersasque obrue puppes**

*incute* (imperat. act., "hurl, drive") – Juno commands Aeolus to unleash force; *vim* (acc. sing., "force, violence") – object of *incute*; *ventis* (dat./abl. pl., "winds") – indirect object or instrument; *submersas* (perf. part. pass. acc. pl. fem., "submerged") modifies *puppes*; *obrue* (imperat. act., "overwhelm, bury") – second command; *puppes* (acc. pl. fem., "ships, sterns") – object of *obrue*. Juno urges violent destruction of the Trojan fleet through storm and shipwreck.

lines.original: aut age diversos et disiice corpora ponto.
lines.english: Or drive them apart and scatter their bodies across the sea.
lines.gloss:
**Target line:** *aut age diversos et disiice corpora ponto.*

**Key words:** *age* (2nd sg. pres. imper. of *ago*) = "drive"; *diversos* (acc. pl. masc. adj.) = "in different directions, scattered"; *disiice* (2nd sg. pres. imper. of *disicio*) = "scatter, disperse"; *corpora* (acc. pl. neut. noun) = "bodies"; *ponto* (abl. sg. masc. of *pontus*) = "over/on the sea."

Juno commands Aeolus either to drive the Trojans apart in different directions and scatter their bodies across the sea, intensifying her demand for their destruction.

lines.original: Sunt mihi bis septem praestanti corpore nymphae,
lines.english: I have twice seven nymphs of surpassing beauty.
lines.gloss: **Sunt** (3rd pl. pres. ind. of *sum*) "there are"; **mihi** (dat. sg. of *ego*) "to me, I have"; **bis septem** "twice seven, fourteen"; **praestanti** (abl. sg. of *praestans, praestantis*, pres. part. of *praesto*) "excelling, outstanding"; **corpore** (abl. sg. of *corpus, corporis*, n.) "in body, in beauty"; **nymphae** (nom. pl. of *nympha*, f.) "nymphs." Juno offers Aeolus fourteen nymphs of surpassing beauty as a bribe to unleash the winds against Aeneas's fleet.

lines.original: quarum quae forma pulcherrima Deiopea,
lines.english: of whom the most beautiful in form is Deiopea
lines.gloss:
**quarum quae forma pulcherrima Deiopea**

*quarum* (gen. pl. fem. of *qui, quae, quod*): "of whom," referring back to the nymphs. *quae* (nom. sg. fem. relative pronoun): "who," introducing the relative clause identifying Deiopea. *forma* (abl. sg. of *forma, -ae* f.): "in beauty/form," ablative of respect. *pulcherrima* (nom. sg. fem. superlative of *pulcher*): "most beautiful." *Deiopea* (nom. sg., Greek name): the nymph Deiopeia, subject of the clause. Juno specifies which nymph is fairest among the fourteen she possesses.

lines.original: conubio iungam stabili propriamque dicabo,
lines.english: I will join in lasting marriage and dedicate as your very own
lines.gloss: **conubio** (noun, dative/ablative singular, "in marriage") **iungam** (verb, 1st sing. future, "I shall join") **stabili** (adjective, dative/ablative singular, "lasting, permanent") **propriam** (adjective, accusative singular feminine, "as your own") **dicabo** (verb, 1st sing. future, "I shall dedicate/assign"). Juno promises to unite Deiopea to Aeolus in permanent wedlock and assign her as his own possession.

lines.original: omnis ut tecum meritis pro talibus annos
lines.english: so that with you she may spend all her years for such deserts
lines.gloss:
**omnis ut tecum meritis pro talibus annos**

*omnis* (acc. pl. m./f., modifying *annos*) "all"; *tecum* (prep. + abl.) "with you"; *meritis* (abl. pl. n., from *meritum*) "for services/deserts"; *pro* (prep. + abl.) "in return for"; *talibus* (abl. pl. n./m./f., from *talis*) "such (great)"; *annos* (acc. pl. m., from *annus*) "years." Dido promises that her consort may spend all his years with her in exchange for such great services.

lines.original: exigat, et pulchra faciat te prole parentem.
lines.english: and make you a parent with beautiful offspring.
lines.gloss: **exigat** (pres. subj., 3rd sg. of *exigo*) "may he pass/spend"; **pulchra** (abl. sg. fem. of *pulcher*) "beautiful," modifying *prole*; **prole** (abl. sg. of *proles*) "offspring/children"; **parentem** (acc. sg. of *parens*) "parent," in apposition to *te*. Juno wishes that the hero may pass all his years with her and that she may make him a parent through beautiful offspring, expressing a blessing of prosperity and dynastic continuity.

lines.original: Tuus, O regina, quid optes Aeolus haec contra:
lines.english: Aeolus replies to you, O queen, as to what you desire:
lines.gloss: **Tuus** (possessive adj., nom. sg. masc.) "yours/your," **O regina** (voc. sg. fem.) "O queen," **quid** (interrog. pron., acc. sg. neut.) "what," **optes** (pres. subjunct., 2nd sg.) "you wish/desire," **Aeolus** (nom. sg. masc.) "Aeolus," **contra** (adv.) "in reply." Aeolus responds to Juno, emphasizing that his duty is to discern and fulfill whatever she, the queen, desires.

lines.original: explorare labor; mihi iussa capessere fas est.
lines.english: Your task is to explore what you desire; for me it is right to undertake your commands.
lines.gloss: **explorare** (pres. act. inf., "to investigate/ascertain") **labor** (nom. sg., "task/duty"), **mihi** (dat. sg., "for me") **iussa** (acc. pl. neut., "commands") **capessere** (pres. act. inf., "to undertake/execute"), **fas** (indecl. nom./acc., "divine law/right"). Aeolus responds to Juno: "Yours is the task to investigate what you wish; for me it is right to undertake your commands," establishing the hierarchical relationship where he merely obeys her divine will.

lines.original: Tu mihi, quodcumque hoc regni, tu sceptra Iovemque
lines.english: You grant me this kingdom, whatever it is, you reconcile me with the scepter and Jupiter.
lines.gloss: **Tu** (pronoun, nominative, "you") **mihi** (pronoun, dative, "to/for me") **quodcumque hoc regni** (pronoun + pronoun + genitive, "whatever of kingdom/this of kingdom") **tu sceptra** (pronoun nominative + accusative plural, "you, the scepters") **Iovemque** (accusative + enclitic, "and Jupiter"). Dido addresses her sister Anna, crediting her with granting whatever royal power she possesses, the symbols of authority (sceptra), and favorable relations with Jupiter; the repetition of *tu* emphasizes Anna's agency as benefactor.

lines.original: concilias, tu das epulis accumbere divom,
lines.english: You win me the favor of Jupiter and his scepter, you grant me to recline at the feasts of the gods.
lines.gloss: **concilias** (2nd sg. pres. act. indic. of *conciliō, -āre*) "you bring into harmony, reconcile"; **das** (2nd sg. pres. act. indic. of *dō, dare*) "you grant, give"; **epulis** (dat./abl. pl. of *epulae, -ārum* f.) "at the feasts"; **accumbere** (pres. act. inf. of *accumbō, -ere*) "to recline"; **divom** (gen. pl. of *deus, -ī* m., archaic form = *divōrum*) "of the gods." Juno continues addressing Aeolus: you reconcile favor, you grant him to recline at the gods' banquets (subject of both verbs remains Jupiter from the previous line).

lines.original: nimborumque facis tempestatumque potentem.
lines.english: and you make him lord of storms and tempests.
lines.gloss:
**nimborumque facis tempestatumque potentem.**

*nimborum* (genitive plural of *nimbus*, "of storms/rainclouds") and *tempestatumque* (genitive plural of *tempestas*, "of tempests/weather") depend on *potentem* (accusative singular adjective, "powerful over/master of"). *facis* (2nd person singular present active indicative of *facio*, "you make") governs *potentem* as object complement, referring to the god being addressed (likely Neptune or another deity). Juno continues her flattery: "you make [him] master of storms and tempests."

lines.original: Haec ubi dicta, cavum conversa cuspide montem
lines.english: Having said these things, he struck the hollow mountain with reversed spear-point.
lines.gloss:
**Haec ubi dicta, cavum conversa cuspide montem**

*Haec* (neut. pl. acc., demonstrative pronoun) "these things"; *dicta* (perf. pass. participle from *dico*, neut. pl. nom./acc.) "having been said"; *cavum* (adj., masc. acc. sg.) "hollow"; *conversa* (perf. pass. participle from *converto*, nom./abl. fem. sg.) "having turned"; *cuspide* (fem. abl. sg., *cuspis*) "with his spear-point"; *montem* (masc. acc. sg., *mons*) "mountain." When these things had been said, Aeolus struck the hollow mountain with his turned spear-point (the ablative absolute *conversa cuspide* indicates the instrument).

lines.original: impulit in latus: ac venti, velut agmine facto,
lines.english: He struck it in the side: and the winds, as if in battle formation drawn up,
lines.gloss:
**impulit in latus: ac venti, velut agmine facto,**

*impulit* (3rd sg. perf. act. indic. of *impello*) "drove/thrust"; *latus* (acc. neut. sg.) "side/flank"; *venti* (nom. masc. pl.) "winds"; *velut* (adv.) "just as/like"; *agmine* (abl. neut. sg. of *agmen*) "battle-line/column," with *facto* (abl. neut. sg. perf. pass. part. of *facio*) "having been formed." Aeolus thrust his spear into the mountain's side, and the winds, as if a battle formation had been formed, rush forth in military array.

lines.original: qua data porta, ruunt et terras turbine perflant.
lines.english: Where a passage is given, they rush forth and sweep the lands with whirlwind.
lines.gloss:
**qua data porta, ruunt et terras turbine perflant.**

*qua* (relative adverb, "where/by which way"), *data* (perfect passive participle from *do*, ablative feminine singular modifying *porta*, "having been given/granted"), *porta* (ablative singular, "gate/opening"), *ruunt* (3rd plural present indicative of *ruo*, "they rush"), *turbine* (ablative singular of *turbo*, "with a whirlwind/storm"), *perflant* (3rd plural present of *perflo*, "they blow through"). The winds rush through the granted opening and blast through the lands with whirlwind force.

lines.original: Incubuere mari, totumque a sedibus imis
lines.english: They brood upon the sea and upheave it whole from its deepest foundations.
lines.gloss:
**Incubuere mari, totumque a sedibus imis**

*Incubuere* (perf. indic. 3rd pl. of *incumbo*) "they press upon/fall upon"; *mari* (dat. sg.) "upon the sea"; *totum* (acc. sg. neut.) "the whole [sea]"; *sedibus* (abl. pl.) "from its seats/foundations"; *imis* (abl. pl. superl. adj.) "deepest/lowest." The winds violently bear down upon the sea and churn it up entirely from its deepest foundations.

lines.original: una Eurusque Notusque ruunt creberque procellis
lines.english: Together East Wind and South Wind rush forth and Southwest Wind thick with storms, and they roll vast waves to the shores.
lines.gloss: **una** (adv.) = together, at once; **Eurus** (nom. m. sg.) = the East wind; **Notus** (nom. m. sg.) = the South wind; **ruunt** (3rd pl. pres. ind. act., *ruo*) = rush, storm forth; **creber** (nom. m. sg.) = thick, frequent; **procellis** (abl. f. pl.) = with storms, squalls. The East and South winds rush forth together, and [another wind] thick with storms—a hendiadys of violent convergence as multiple winds assault the sea simultaneously.

lines.original: Africus, et vastos volvunt ad litora fluctus.
lines.english: and the southwest wind, and they roll vast waves toward the shores.
lines.gloss: **Africus** (nom. sg., subject) "the southwest wind," **vastos** (acc. pl. masc., modifying *fluctus*) "vast, huge," **volvunt** (3rd pl. pres. act. ind.) "roll, drive," **litora** (acc. pl. neut.) "shores," **fluctus** (acc. pl. masc., direct object) "waves." The southwest wind joins the East and South winds in rolling massive waves toward the shore, completing the catalog of storm winds unleashed by Aeolus.

lines.original: Insequitur clamorque virum stridorque rudentum.
lines.english: There follows the shouting of men and the shrieking of the rigging.
lines.gloss: **Insequitur** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. ind., "follows upon" or "ensues") **clamorque** (noun, nom. sg. with -que, "and the shouting") **virum** (noun, gen. pl., "of men") **stridorque** (noun, nom. sg. with -que, "and the screeching/whistling") **rudentum** (noun, gen. pl., "of the ropes/rigging"). The storm's violence is immediately followed by the clamor of sailors and the shrieking of the ship's rigging under strain.

lines.original: Eripiunt subito nubes caelumque diemque
lines.english: Suddenly the clouds snatch away both sky and daylight.
lines.gloss: **Eripiunt** (3rd pl. pres. act. ind., *eripio*) "snatch away"; **subito** (adv.) "suddenly"; **nubes** (nom. pl., *nubes*) "clouds" (subject); **caelumque diemque** (acc. pl., *caelum* and *dies*, connected by *-que*...*-que*) "both sky and daylight" (objects of *eripiunt*). The clouds suddenly snatch away both sky and daylight from the Trojans' eyes, as the storm erupts.

lines.original: Teucrorum ex oculis; ponto nox incubat atra.
lines.english: from the eyes of the Trojans; black night settles upon the sea.
lines.gloss: **Teucrorum** (gen. pl., "of the Trojans/Teucrians") **ex oculis** (abl. pl., "from the eyes") **ponto** (dat./abl. sg., "on the sea") **nox** (nom. sg., "night") **incubat** (3rd sg. pres., "lies upon/broods over") **atra** (nom. sg. fem., "black/dark"). The clouds snatch sky and daylight from the Trojans' sight; black night settles upon the sea.

lines.original: Intonuere poli, et crebris micat ignibus aether,
lines.english: The heavens thundered and the sky flashed with constant fires.
lines.gloss: **Intonuere** (perf. ind. act., 3rd pl. of *intono*) "thundered" – the heavens resounded. **poli** (nom. pl., *polus*) "the heavens/skies" – subject of the verb. **crebris ignibus** (abl. pl., *creber* + *ignis*) "with frequent fires/flashes" – describes the lightning. **micat** (pres. ind. act., 3rd sg. of *mico*) "flashes/gleams" – **aether** (nom. sg., *aether*) "the upper air/sky" – flashes with repeated lightning bolts. The heavens thunder and the sky flashes with constant lightning, intensifying the storm's fury.

lines.original: praesentemque viris intentant omnia mortem.
lines.english: All things threaten the men with death close at hand.
lines.gloss:
**praesentemque viris intentant omnia mortem.**

*praesentem* (adj., acc. sg. f.) modifying *mortem*, "immediate" or "present"; *viris* (noun, dat. pl. m.) "for the men"; *intentant* (verb, 3rd pl. pres. act. indic.) "threaten" or "portend"; *omnia* (adj./pron., nom. pl. n.) "all things" serving as subject; *mortem* (noun, acc. sg. f.) "death." All things threaten immediate death to the men, as the storm's fury portends their imminent destruction.

lines.original: Extemplo Aeneae solvuntur frigore membra:
lines.english: At once Aeneas's limbs go slack with cold dread.
lines.gloss:
**Extemplo Aeneae solvuntur frigore membra:**

*Extemplo* (adv., "immediately"), *Aeneae* (gen. sg., "of Aeneas"), *solvuntur* (pres. pass. indic. 3rd pl., "are loosened/grow weak"), *frigore* (abl. sg., "with/by cold/chill"), *membra* (nom. pl. neut., "limbs"). Immediately Aeneas' limbs grow weak with cold—a vivid description of the physical effects of sudden terror as he faces the storm at sea.

lines.original: ingemit, et duplicis tendens ad sidera palmas
lines.english: He groans, and stretching his upraised palms twice toward the stars
lines.gloss:
**ingemit, et duplicis tendens ad sidera palmas**

*ingemit* (3rd sg. pres. ind. of *ingemo*) "he groans"; *duplicis* (acc. pl. f. of *duplex*) "double, both"; *tendens* (pres. part. of *tendo*) "stretching, extending"; *sidera* (acc. pl. n. of *sidus*) "stars, heavens"; *palmas* (acc. pl. f. of *palma*) "palms, hands." Aeneas groans and stretches both hands toward the stars in a gesture of supplication or despair.

lines.original: O terque quaterque beati, talia voce refert:
lines.english: O three and four times blessed, he speaks such words:
lines.gloss:
**Target:** *O terque quaterque beati, talia voce refert:*

**terque quaterque** (adverbs) "three and four times" = seven times, emphatically "many times over"; **beati** (nominative plural adjective/substantive) "blessed ones, fortunate ones"; **talia** (neuter plural accusative, demonstrative pronoun) "such things"; **voce** (ablative singular of *vox*) "with his voice"; **refert** (3rd singular present indicative of *referre*) "he speaks, utters." Aeneas addresses those who died at Troy as supremely fortunate, introducing his lament with ritualized emphasis.

lines.original: quis ante ora patrum Troiae sub moenibus altis
lines.english: whom it befell to die before their fathers' eyes beneath the high walls of Troy!
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for "quis ante ora patrum Troiae sub moenibus altis":**

*quis* (relative/interrogative pronoun, dative plural) "for whom"; *ante* (preposition + accusative) "before"; *ora* (noun, accusative plural, n. of *os*) "faces, presence"; *patrum* (noun, genitive plural of *pater*) "of fathers, ancestors"; *moenibus altis* (noun + adjective, ablative plural) "beneath the lofty walls." Aeneas continues his apostrophe, identifying those blessed who died before their fathers' eyes beneath Troy's towering fortifications.

lines.original: contigit oppetere! O Danaum fortissime gentis
lines.english: who was granted to meet death before his father's eyes! O bravest of the Greek race
lines.gloss:
**contigit oppetere! O Danaum fortissime gentis**

*contigit* (3rd sing. perf. ind. of *contingō*) = "it befell, was granted"; *oppetere* (pres. act. inf. of *oppetō*) = "to meet death, perish"; *Danaum* (gen. pl. of *Danaī*) = "of the Greeks"; *fortissime* (voc. sing. masc. superl. of *fortis*) = "O bravest"; *gentis* (gen. sing. of *gēns*) = "of the race, people." 

Aeneas laments that Diomedes, the bravest of the Greeks, was granted the privilege of dying gloriously at Troy, unlike his own inglorious fate of shipwreck.

lines.original: Tydide! Mene Iliacis occumbere campis
lines.english: O son of Tydeus, why could I not have fallen on the Trojan plains
lines.gloss: **Tydide!** (vocative singular of *Tydides*) "son of Tydeus" = Diomedes; **Mene** (accusative singular of *ego* + enclitic *-ne*) "me" (interrogative); **Iliacis** (ablative plural of *Iliacus, -a, -um*) "Trojan"; **occumbere** (present infinitive of *occumbo*) "to fall in death, to die"; **campis** (ablative plural of *campus*) "on the plains." Aeneas laments that he could not die by Diomedes' hand on the Trojan plains, an honorable death befitting a warrior.

lines.original: non potuisse, tuaque animam hanc effundere dextra,
lines.english: that I could not have fallen and poured out this life by your right hand
lines.gloss: **non potuisse** (perfect active infinitive of *possum*): "to have been unable," expressing the regret that she could not die at Troy. **tuaque ... dextra** (ablative of means with *tua*, "your"): "by your right hand," referring to Diomedes' weapon. **animam** (accusative singular of *anima*): "life" or "soul," the object of *effundere*. **effundere** (perfect active infinitive of *effundo*): "to pour out," i.e., to give up in death. Dido laments that she was not permitted to fall on the Trojan plains and surrender her life to Diomedes' spear.

lines.original: saevus ubi Aeacidae telo iacet Hector, ubi ingens
lines.english: where fierce Hector lies slain by the spear of Aeacides, where mighty
lines.gloss: **saevus** (adj., nom. sg. m.) "fierce/savage"; **Aeacidae** (noun, gen. sg. m.) "of the descendant of Aeacus" (i.e., Achilles); **telo** (noun, abl. sg. n.) "by the weapon/spear"; **iacet** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. ind.) "lies (dead)"; **Hector** (proper noun, nom. sg. m.) "Hector." The speaker laments where fierce Hector lies slain by the weapon of Achilles, continuing a catalog of places associated with Trojan deaths, introduced by the repeated "ubi."

lines.original: Sarpedon, ubi tot Simois correpta sub undis
lines.english: where mighty Sarpedon lies, where the Simois rolls so many shields and helmets of men and brave bodies seized beneath its waves
lines.gloss: **Sarpedon** (nom. sg., proper name) – Sarpedon, the Lycian hero and son of Zeus slain by Patroclus; **tot** (indecl. adj.) – so many; **Simois** (nom. sg., proper name) – the Simoïs, river at Troy; **correpta** (perf. pass. part., nom./acc. pl. n.) – seized, snatched away; **sub undis** (abl. pl. with prep.) – beneath the waves. The line continues the catalog of Trojan casualties, asking where Sarpedon lies and noting how many shields and helmets the Simoïs river has swept beneath its waters.

lines.original: scuta virum galeasque et fortia corpora volvit?
lines.english: where the Simois rolls shields of men and helmets and brave bodies beneath its waves
lines.gloss: **scuta** (n. acc. pl., < *scutum*) "shields"; **virum** (gen. pl., < *vir*) "of men"; **galeasque** (acc. pl., < *galea*) "and helmets"; **fortia corpora** (acc. pl., neut. adj. + n., < *fortis* + *corpus*) "strong/brave bodies"; **volvit** (3rd sg. pres., < *volvo*) "rolls/tosses." The Simois river rolls along shields, helmets, and the brave bodies of warriors swept beneath its waves.

lines.original: Talia iactanti stridens Aquilone procella
lines.english: While he hurls such words, a storm shrieking with the North Wind strikes the sail head-on and lifts the waves to the stars.
lines.gloss:
**Talia iactanti stridens Aquilone procella**

*Talia* (neut. acc. pl., "such things") is the object of *iactanti* (pres. act. part., dat./abl. sg. from *iacio*, "hurling/shouting"), referring to Aeneas speaking. *Stridens* (pres. act. part., nom. sg. from *strido*, "shrieking/whistling") modifies *procella* (nom. sg., "storm"), the subject. *Aquilone* (abl. sg., "from the North Wind" or "with the North Wind") indicates origin or accompaniment. The storm shrieks from the north upon Aeneas as he utters such words.

lines.original: velum adversa ferit, fluctusque ad sidera tollit.
lines.english: It strikes the sail head-on and lifts the waves to the stars.
lines.gloss: **velum** (n., acc. sg.) "sail" – object of *ferit*; **adversa** (adj., nom. sg. fem.) "head-on" or "opposing" – modifying *procella* from the previous line; **ferit** (v., 3rd sg. pres.) "strikes"; **fluctusque** (n., acc. pl.) "and the waves" – object of *tollit*; **sidera** (n., acc. pl.) "stars" – limit of motion with *ad*; **tollit** (v., 3rd sg. pres.) "lifts/raises." The storm strikes the sail head-on and lifts the waves up to the stars, depicting the tempest's violent force.

lines.original: Franguntur remi; tum prora avertit, et undis
lines.english: The oars are shattered; then the prow turns away, and to the waves exposes its side.
lines.gloss: **Franguntur** (*frangō*, 3rd pl. pres. pass. ind.) "are shattered/broken" — the oars snap under strain. **remi** (nom. pl. m.) "oars." **prora** (nom. sg. f.) "prow/bow" — the front of the ship. **avertit** (*āvertō*, 3rd sg. pres. act. ind.) "turns away" — the bow swings around. **undis** (dat./abl. pl. f.) "to/for the waves" — presenting the ship's vulnerable side to the sea's assault.

lines.original: dat latus; insequitur cumulo praeruptus aquae mons.
lines.english: The ship turns broadside to the waves; a towering mountain of water follows in a heap.
lines.gloss:
**dat latus; insequitur cumulo praeruptus aquae mons.**

*dat* (3rd sg. pres. act. ind. of *do*) "gives, exposes"; *latus* (n. acc. sg.) "side, flank"; *insequitur* (3rd sg. pres. dep. ind. of *insequor*) "follows, pursues"; *praeruptus* (nom. sg. m. perf. pass. part.) "steep, headlong"; *mons* (nom. sg. m.) "mountain, mass." The ship exposes its vulnerable side to the waves, and a towering, sheer mountain of water follows in a heap upon it.

lines.original: Hi summo in fluctu pendent; his unda dehiscens
lines.english: These hang on the wave's crest; for these the yawning water reveals the earth between the waves.
lines.gloss:
**Hi summo in fluctu pendent; his unda dehiscens**

*Hi* (nom. pl. m., "these men/ships") and *his* (dat. pl. m., "for these") establish antithesis between two groups of sailors. *Summo in fluctu* (abl. sg. m., "on the highest wave") locates the first group at the crest. *Pendent* (3rd pl. pres. act. indic. of *pendeo*, "hang, are suspended") describes their precarious position. *Unda dehiscens* (nom. sg. f., "the gaping wave" – pres. act. participle of *dehisco*, "gape open, split apart") introduces the opposite peril facing the second group in the wave's trough.

lines.original: terram inter fluctus aperit; furit aestus harenis.
lines.english: The wave opening reveals the earth between the surges; the tide rages with sand.
lines.gloss: **terram** (acc. sing. f., "land/ground"), **inter** (prep. + acc., "between/amid"), **fluctus** (acc. pl. m., "waves"), **aperit** (pres. 3rd sing., "opens/reveals"), **furit** (pres. 3rd sing., "rages"), **aestus** (nom. sing. m., "surge/boiling"), **harenis** (abl. pl. f., "with sands/in the sands"). The wave opens up the land between the waters, and the surge boils furiously with sand churned up from the seabed.

lines.original: Tris Notus abreptas in saxa latentia torquet—
lines.english: The South Wind whirls three ships swept away onto hidden rocks.
lines.gloss:
**Tris Notus abreptas in saxa latentia torquet—**

*Tris* (acc. pl. adj., "three"), *Notus* (nom. sg., "the South Wind," subject), *abreptas* (acc. pl. f. perf. pass. part. from *abripio*, modifying ships understood, "snatched away"), *latentia* (acc. pl. n. pres. act. part. from *lateo*, modifying *saxa*, "hidden/lurking"), *torquet* (3rd sg. pres. act. indic., "twists/hurls"). The South Wind hurls three ships, snatched away by the storm, onto hidden rocks.

lines.original: saxa vocant Itali mediis quae in fluctibus aras—
lines.english: The Italians call these rocks altars which lie in the midst of the waves.
lines.gloss:
**saxa vocant Itali mediis quae in fluctibus aras—**

*saxa* (n. acc. pl., "rocks"); *vocant* (3rd pl. pres. act., "call"); *Itali* (m. nom. pl., "the Italians"); *mediis...in fluctibus* (abl. pl., "in the midst of the waves"); *aras* (f. acc. pl., "altars"). The Italians call these rocks "the Altars," which lie in the middle of the waves—a notorious reef formation.

lines.original: dorsum immane mari summo; tris Eurus ab alto
lines.english: a massive ridge on the sea's surface; the East Wind from the deep drives three ships
lines.gloss:
**dorsum immane mari summo; tris Eurus ab alto**

*dorsum* (n. acc. sg.) "back, reef" – the submerged rocky ridge; *immane* (adj. acc. sg. n.) "monstrous, huge" modifying *dorsum*; *mari summo* (abl. sg.) "on the surface of the sea"; *tris* = *teris* (2nd sg. pres. indic.) "you grind, wear away"; *Eurus* (nom. sg.) "the East wind" as subject; *ab alto* (abl. sg.) "from the deep." The East wind grinds ships upon the monstrous reef lying just beneath the sea's surface.

lines.original: in brevia et Syrtis urguet, miserabile visu,
lines.english: drives them into the shallows and Syrtes, a pitiable sight, and dashes them on shoals and girds them round with a sandbank.
lines.gloss:
**Target: in brevia et Syrtis urguet, miserabile visu,**

*brevia* (n. acc. pl., "shallows, shoals"), *Syrtis* (f. acc. pl., "the Syrtes," sandbanks off North Africa), *urguet* (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of *urgeo*, "drives, forces"), *miserabile* (n. acc. sg. adj., "pitiable, wretched"), *visu* (m. abl. sg. supine of *video*, "to see," in ablative of respect). Eurus drives [the ships] into the shallows and Syrtes—a sight pitiable to behold.

lines.original: inliditque vadis atque aggere cingit harenae.
lines.english: and dashes them on the shoals and encircles them with a mound of sand.
lines.gloss:
**inliditque vadis atque aggere cingit harenae.**

*inlidit* (3rd sg. pres. indic. act. of *illido*) "dashes upon"; *vadis* (abl. pl. of *vadum*) "shallows, shoals"; *aggere* (abl. sg. of *agger*) "mound, heap"; *cingit* (3rd sg. pres. indic. act. of *cingo*) "surrounds, encircles"; *harenae* (gen. sg. of *harena*) "of sand." The ship is dashed upon the shallows and surrounded by a mound of sand, describing its grounding and entrapment.

lines.original: Unam, quae Lycios fidumque vehebat Oronten,
lines.english: One ship, which was carrying the Lycians and faithful Orontes,
lines.gloss:
**Unam, quae Lycios fidumque vehebat Oronten,**

*Unam* (acc. fem. sing. of *unus*, "one [ship]") is the direct object. *quae* (nom. fem. sing. relative pronoun, "which") introduces a relative clause. *Lycios* (acc. masc. pl. of *Lycius*, "Lycians") and *Oronten* (acc. masc. sing., "Orontes") are both objects of *vehebat* (imperf. act. indic. 3rd sing. of *veho*, "was carrying"). *fidum* (acc. masc. sing. of *fidus*, "faithful/loyal") modifies *Oronten*.

lines.original: ipsius ante oculos ingens a vertice pontus
lines.english: A huge wave from its crest strikes before his very eyes upon the stern.
lines.gloss:
**ipsius ante oculos ingens a vertice pontus**

*ipsius* (gen. sing. of *ipse*) "of him himself" (i.e., Aeneas); *ante oculos* (prep. + acc. pl.) "before the eyes"; *ingens* (nom. sing. adj.) "huge, massive"; *a vertice* (prep. + abl. sing.) "from the crest/top"; *pontus* (nom. sing.) "sea, wave." Before Aeneas's very eyes, a massive wave strikes from its crest, introducing the catastrophic blow that follows in the next line.

lines.original: in puppim ferit: excutitur pronusque magister
lines.english: It strikes the stern: the helmsman is hurled out and rolled headlong.
lines.gloss:
**in puppim ferit: excutitur pronusque magister**

*puppim* (acc. sg. of *puppis*, f.) = "stern" (of the ship); *ferit* (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of *ferio*) = "strikes"; *excutitur* (3rd sg. pres. pass. indic. of *excutio*) = "is hurled out/shaken off"; *pronusque* = "and headlong" (*pronus*, nom. sg. m., modifying *magister*); *magister* (nom. sg. m.) = "helmsman." The wave strikes the stern, and the helmsman is violently thrown out headlong.

lines.original: volvitur in caput; ast illam ter fluctus ibidem
lines.english: is hurled headlong; but the wave whirls the ship thrice round in the same place and the swift whirlpool swallows it in the sea.
lines.gloss:
**volvitur in caput; ast illam ter fluctus ibidem**

*volvitur* (3rd sg. pres. pass. ind. of *volvo*) "is rolled/tumbled," the helmsman spins headlong; *caput* (acc. sg. n.) "head," indicating the direction of his fall; *ast* (conj.) "but," marking the shift to the ship's fate; *fluctus* (nom. sg. m.) "wave/billow," subject of the following action; *ter* (adv.) "three times," emphasizing the repetition of the wave's battering; *ibidem* (adv.) "in the same place," the ship trapped in one spot.

lines.original: torquet agens circum, et rapidus vorat aequore vortex.
lines.english: The driving wave spins it around and the swift whirlpool devours it in the sea.
lines.gloss: **torquet** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. ind.) "twists/whirls"; **agens** (verb, pres. part. nom. sg.) "driving"; **circum** (adv.) "around/in a circle"; **rapidus** (adj. nom. sg. m.) "swift/raging"; **vorat** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. ind.) "devours/swallows up"; **vortex** (noun, nom. sg. m.) "whirlpool/vortex". The swift whirlpool twists and drives the ship around in circles, then devours it in the sea.

lines.original: Adparent rari nantes in gurgite vasto,
lines.english: A few men swimming appear scattered in the vast whirlpool.
lines.gloss: **Adparent** (3rd pl. pres. ind. of *adpareo*) "appear," **rari** (nom. pl. masc. adj.) "scattered/few," **nantes** (nom. pl. masc. pres. part. of *no*) "swimming," **gurgite** (abl. sg. of *gurges*) "in the whirlpool/abyss," **vasto** (abl. sg. masc. adj.) "vast/enormous." A few scattered swimmers appear in the vast whirlpool, describing survivors struggling in the sea after the shipwreck.

lines.original: arma virum, tabulaeque, et Troia gaza per undas.
lines.english: Arms of men, planks, and Trojan treasure through the waves.
lines.gloss: **arma** (n. nom./acc. pl., "arms, equipment"), **virum** (gen. pl., "of men"), **tabulae** (nom. pl., "planks, timbers"), **gaza** (nom. sg., "treasure, wealth"), **undas** (acc. pl., "waves"). The scattered debris of the Trojan fleet becomes visible: weapons, men's gear, ship planks, and Trojan treasure are seen floating through the waves after the storm's destruction.

lines.original: Iam validam Ilionei navem, iam fortis Achati,
lines.english: Now the sturdy ship of Ilioneus, now that of brave Achates.
lines.gloss:
**Iam validam Ilionei navem, iam fortis Achati,**

*validam* (adj., acc. sg. fem.) "strong"; *Ilionei* (proper noun, gen. sg.) "of Ilioneus"; *navem* (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "ship"; *fortis* (adj., gen. sg. masc.) "brave/strong"; *Achati* (proper noun, gen. sg.) "of Achates." The storm now assails the sturdy ship of Ilioneus and that of brave Achates, with possessive genitives marking the vessels' ownership by these Trojan companions.

lines.original: et qua vectus Abas, et qua grandaevus Aletes,
lines.english: and the ship that carried Abas and the one that carried aged Aletes
lines.gloss:
**et qua vectus Abas, et qua grandaevus Aletes,**

*vectus* (perf. pass. part. of *veho*, nom. sg. masc.) "having been carried"; *Abas* (nom. sg.) the Trojan hero Abas; *qua* (abl. sg. fem. of *qui*) "in/on which" (sc. *nave*); *grandaevus* (adj., nom. sg. masc.) "aged, venerable"; *Aletes* (nom. sg.) the elderly Trojan Aletes. The anaphoric *et qua...et qua* construction parallels the ships carrying Abas and old Aletes, both now overcome by the storm.

lines.original: vicit hiems; laxis laterum compagibus omnes
lines.english: The storm prevailed; all ships with loosened joints in their sides take in the hostile water and gape open at the seams.
lines.gloss:
**vicit hiems; laxis laterum compagibus omnes**

*vicit* (perf. act. ind. 3rd sg. of *vinco*) "conquered, prevailed"; *hiems* (nom. sg. f.) "the storm, winter weather"; *laxis* (abl. pl. f. of *laxus*) "loosened, slack"; *laterum* (gen. pl. n. of *latus*) "of the sides"; *compagibus* (abl. pl. f. of *compages*) "joints, fastenings." The storm has conquered; all the ships' side-fastenings having been loosened, they receive the hostile rain and split apart at the seams.

lines.original: accipiunt inimicum imbrem, rimisque fatiscunt.
lines.english: They all take in the hostile rain through loosened joints and gape open with cracks.
lines.gloss:
**accipiunt inimicum imbrem, rimisque fatiscunt.**

Key words: *accipiunt* (3rd pl. pres. act. ind., "they receive"), *inimicum* (acc. sg. masc. adj., "hostile/harmful"), *imbrem* (acc. sg. masc., "rain/water"), *rimis* (abl. pl. fem., "through cracks"), *fatiscunt* (3rd pl. pres. act. ind., "they gape open/fall apart"). The ships take on destructive seawater through their loosened seams and split apart at the cracks.

lines.original: Interea magno misceri murmure pontum,
lines.english: Meanwhile Neptune sensed the sea churning with a great roar and the storm let loose.
lines.gloss: **Interea** (adv., "meanwhile") **magno** (adj., abl. sing. masc./neut., "great/loud," modifying *murmure*) **misceri** (pres. pass. inf., "to be stirred up/thrown into confusion") **murmure** (noun, abl. sing., "roar/rumbling," ablative of manner) **pontum** (noun, acc. sing., "sea/deep," subject of the infinitive). Meanwhile the sea is stirred up with a great roar; this indirect statement introduces Neptune's awareness of the storm Aeolus has unleashed at Juno's command.

lines.original: emissamque hiemem sensit Neptunus, et imis
lines.english: Neptune sensed the unleashed storm and the waters driven up from the lowest depths, and deeply disturbed
lines.gloss:
**emissamque hiemem sensit Neptunus, et imis**

*emissam* (perf. pass. partic., acc. fem. sing. from *emitto*) "sent forth, unleashed"; *hiemem* (acc. fem. sing.) "storm, winter tempest"; *sensit* (perf. 3rd sing. from *sentio*) "perceived, felt"; *Neptunus* (nom. masc. sing.) "Neptune" (god of the sea); *imis* (abl. neut. plur. from *imus*) "from the depths." Neptune perceived that the storm had been unleashed, introducing the sea-god's awareness of Aeolus's interference with his domain.

lines.original: stagna refusa vadis, graviter commotus; et alto
lines.english: the pools stirred up from the lowest shallows, deeply moved; and from the deep
lines.gloss:
**stagna refusa vadis, graviter commotus; et alto**
